"Soldiers! Today is the day! We will leave the Tree of Life and begin our journey to eradicate the Flora once and for all!" Commander Hua Bing shouted from the top of his lungs. "Regular Chlora are allowed to come with and rest at the base camps we will be setting up. Once we near the Flora however, they will not be allowed any further."

Jiu Xing heard the declaration, as had everyone else. Chlora were frantic today, packing up goods if they were leaving, or selling in the markets if they were staying. Jiu knew what she was going to do, she had already set her mind upon it. The only problem she would have would be convincing her parents to let her go follow the soldiers and live at the base camps. She walked out of her room, that had all her belongings and food bagged up into a pile.

"Mom, a few of my friends are going to live at the base camps, can I go with them?" Jiu asked in her most sincere voice.

"Absolutely not! I don't want you anywhere close to where the Flora will be. They are a destructive species that can only spell trouble." Ma Ma Xing retorted.

"I promise I'll stick with adults there, and won't get into any trouble!" Jiu tried to make her eyes look like that of a innocent puppy, hoping to get an emotional response out of her.

"I've already said no young lady! You father will agree with me on this! Now I want you to stop asking me if you can go and go have fun with your friends before they leave." Ma Ma Xing strictly said back.

"But mom, please can I go?" Jiu's eyes started to tear, and moments later she was full out bawling on the floor in tears.

"Jiu, I've said no. Now go have fun for the rest of the day." Ma Ma Xing tried to comfort her without looking as if she wasn't caving in to her wishes.

"Fine, I'll go have *fun* while they all leave me..." Jiu got up an walked away, sulking, hoping this final attempt would get her mom to say yes. But alas, it proved all for not.

----------

Later that night, once the family had gone to sleep, Jiu knew what she was going to do, and was deeply sorry for it. She placed her bagged supplies outside her window first, then climbed out with them. She took a wagon from a nearby stall that was empty for the night. Inside the wagon was a bow with a couple of arrows, some rope, and a map of the continent the Tree of Life was on, marked where the soldiers were headed. Jiu placed her supplies on the wagon, and took the map. She held both handles, and began her journey west to the first base camp, Yicun, the first stop on her journey.

I love KDE but I think they are insane using cutting-edge and stable on the same phrase.

As a developer I know getting the source code directly fresh from the GIT repository is far from stable. There is a reason why users usually have to wait weeks or months before they get updates- it's just the time it takes to verify software is good plus some management overhead.

This as all fine and dandy until Neon starts imposing developers should have 100% stable software on their master GIT branches. This is not how open-source software works, especially if people are doing it on their free time. If it comes to this it could be a big hit on the KDE ecosystem.

The interview link at the end has more info.

I am not a developer and so could be radically misunderstanding this but I don't think Neon is going to be using the untested/unproven KDE software. When I run Kubuntu, I pretty much am stuck with whatever version of the KDE Plasma Desktop that was used for the Kubuntu release I am on until another 6 months (or 2 years) role by, no matter what stable version has been pushed out since.

I think Neon is aiming to make updating the Plasma Desktop (& other KDE software/packages) as easy as updating Firefox; whenever Plasma 5.whatever is stable, it will get packaged into the Neon repository (or whatever the proper term is) and then installed onto my system like any other package.

But like I said, I am not a dev, just an end user so I could be completely wrong.

My understanding from the interview is that they will get whatever is on the GIT repositories and deliver it to the users when they update, probably with new versions on a daily basis (continuous integration). This means that it's up to every project manager for every single KDE project to make absolutely sure that their latest version is stable (on the master branch of their repositories at least, not necessarily on development branches). This is one hell of a thing to ask for as any developer can tell you, especially for people who are working on these projects for fun or humanitarian reasons.

I will repeat what I said before: if it was this easy to keep software up-to-date why wouldn't Ubuntu and other hundreds of Linux distributions work in exactly the same way, using the projects GIT repositories instead of going through all the extra work and expenses of having and maintaining their own unified repositories?

Again, as I said it's all fine and dandy if Neon users understand they are up to one hell of a ride but if they start expecting every cutting-edge version to function stably as a unified system then I can see a lot of open-source contributors, developers and projects managers saying "I didn't sign up for this shit" and leaving their awesome projects behind. But to be honest they'd just probably keep working the way they do and completely ignore Neon.
